title: Explain and defend a technical trade-off
summary: Recommend an engineering option, make consequences audible and repair an unclear explanation.

sections.title: Decision context
sections.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. Synchronous validation gives an immediate answer but adds up to 900 ms at peak. A queued worker keeps requests fast and retries transient failures, but final status may take two minutes. The release needs predictable request latency; compliance requires validation before publication.

exercises.question: Which requirement favors the queued worker?
exercises.explanation: The queue moves validation latency out of the request path.

performanceTask.title: Recommend and defend one design
performanceTask.scenario: Explain an architecture recommendation to engineers and a product manager.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: In 60–90 seconds, use the decision evidence shown here and state the constraint, recommendation, cost and mitigation before support appears.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: In 60–90 seconds, frame the decision, recommend one option, connect the benefit and cost to constraints, then mitigate the main risk.
performanceTask.modelResponse: I recommend the queued worker because predictable request latency is the deciding release constraint. The synchronous option gives immediate status, but it adds nine hundred milliseconds at peak. By contrast, the queue keeps the request fast and supports retries for transient failures. The main cost is that the final result can remain pending for up to two minutes, so acceptance must not look like completion. I would mitigate that cost by showing a clear pending state and blocking publication until validation succeeds. For this release, that balance protects latency and the validation requirement; if immediate final status became the deciding constraint, we would need to revisit the choice.

audio.text: The request stays fast, but the result is delayed.
I recommend the queued worker because latency is the constraint.
It retries failures; however, users wait for final status.
We can mitigate the delay with a pending state.
